newsitem.title: FRANCE: Credit Lyonnais sees 17,000 less staff by 2000.
newsitem.headline: Credit Lyonnais sees 17,000 less staff by 2000.

text.p: Credit Lyonnais chairman Jean Peyrelevade said on Friday he expected to see staff at the state-owned bank reduced "to less than 40,000 by the turn of the century" from 57,000 at the moment.
A staff reduction plan presented at the end of 1996 will see employment at the beleaguered bank reduced by the equivalent of 9,000 full-time staff.
Peyrelevade told reporters at a press lunch his aim was to arrive at a level of more than one billion francs in net banking income per head, based on a total net banking income of 45 billion francs.
"The staff reduction will not be far off 50 percent compared to when I arrived," he said.

"The Credit Lyonnais of tomorrow will be different to the Credit Lyonnais of today, it's the only way out. It will no longer be a universal bank which thinks it can do everything all over the world," he said.
"It has to learn to be modest," he added, adding that the bank would, like its rivals, focus on retail banking in France and wholesale banking abroad.
He declined to comment in press reports that Credit Lyonnais could part with its European subsidiaries outside France.

Questioned on Credito Bergamasco, it said that at this stage no decisions had been taken and that there were no talks with any Italian banks about a possible divestment, pending talks between the French government and the European Commission in Brussels about a new rescue plan for the group.

Credit Lyonnais ran up some 21 billion francs of losses in 1992-94 after runaway expansion in the 1980s but has failed to pull fully out of trouble after 1994 and 1995 rescue packages and a fresh package is being drawn up.
The latest plan requires clearance from the Commission in Brussels and divestments will be sought in return.
